title: VPC fundamentals
topic: Public/private subnets, IGW, NAT, SG vs NACL, bastion vs SSM, VPC endpoints
format: 10 timed scenario questions (~16 min, ~96 sec each). Answer without peeking at night-8-quiz-answers.json first.
answerDistribution: A×3 B×2 C×3 D×2 — options shuffled so correct letter varies

questions.question: An engineer creates subnets named "public-a" and "private-b" but both route tables only have a local route for 10.0.0.0/16. Neither subnet can reach the internet. What must be added to make subnet public-a actually public?

options.A: Enable auto-assign private IPv4 on the subnet
options.B: Add 0.0.0.0/0 → Internet Gateway to public-a's route table
options.C: Attach a NAT Gateway to public-a
options.D: Change the NACL from default to custom

questions.question: ECS Fargate tasks in a private subnet must pull container images from ECR without sending that traffic through a NAT Gateway. Which combination meets the requirement?

options.A: Internet Gateway in the private subnet route table
options.B: Bastion host in the public subnet with ECR credentials
options.C: Interface endpoints for ecr.api and ecr.dkr plus an S3 gateway endpoint

questions.question: A security group allows inbound HTTPS on port 443 to an EC2 instance. A custom subnet NACL allows inbound 443 but denies all ephemeral ports (1024–65535). Clients cannot complete TLS handshakes. What is the most likely cause?

options.A: NACLs are stateless; return traffic on ephemeral ports is blocked
options.B: Security groups are stateless and require explicit outbound rules for every response port
options.C: The instance needs a public IP for HTTPS

questions.question: You deploy a NAT Gateway so Fargate tasks in private subnets can reach the internet for software updates. Where must the NAT Gateway be placed?

options.B: Any subnet; NAT is VPC-scoped like the Internet Gateway
options.C: Private subnet with no default route to avoid exposure
options.D: Public subnet whose route table has 0.0.0.0/0 → Internet Gateway

questions.question: A Fargate task runs in a private subnet with outbound routing via NAT Gateway. The task security group allows no inbound rules. Can a user on the public internet initiate an SSH session to the task's private IP?

options.A: Yes, if the NAT Gateway forwards inbound connections to matching private IPs
options.B: No; NAT provides outbound-only internet access from the private subnet's perspective
options.C: Yes, if the task execution role has ssm:StartSession
options.D: Yes, after adding an Internet Gateway route to the private subnet

questions.question: A data pipeline in private subnets writes large objects frequently to S3 in the same Region. NAT Gateway data-processing charges are high. What is the most cost-effective networking change for S3 traffic?

options.A: Move the tasks to a public subnet with public IPs
options.B: Add a second NAT Gateway per Availability Zone
options.C: Add an S3 gateway VPC endpoint and route S3 prefix lists to it in the private route table
options.D: Replace the NAT Gateway with a Site-to-Site VPN

questions.question: Administrators need occasional shell access to EC2 instances in private subnets without exposing every instance to the internet. A small EC2 in a public subnet accepts SSH only from the corporate office IP range; private instances accept SSH only from that server's security group. What is this pattern called?

Security wants admin shell access to private EC2 instances without opening port 22 to the internet and without managing SSH keys on a jump box. Instances already run the SSM Agent. What should you use?

options.D: AWS Client VPN with full tunnel only

questions.question: A Lambda function runs inside a VPC in private subnets and calls DynamoDB in the same Region. You want to avoid NAT Gateway charges for DynamoDB traffic. What is the best approach?

options.A: Assign elastic IPs to each Lambda ENI
options.B: Route 0.0.0.0/0 from the Lambda subnets to an Internet Gateway
options.C: Use an Application Load Balancer in front of DynamoDB
options.D: Add a DynamoDB gateway VPC endpoint and update the subnet route tables

questions.question: Aurora PostgreSQL runs in private subnets. A Lambda function in the same VPC must connect on port 5432. Both use security groups. What is the recommended ingress rule on the Aurora security group?

options.A: Allow inbound TCP 5432 from the Lambda function's security group ID
options.C: Allow inbound TCP 5432 from the VPC CIDR 10.0.0.0/16 only
options.D: No inbound rule; Aurora initiates connections to Lambda
